skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Browser automation for AI agents through inference.sh. It opens web pages, exposes compact element refs, performs browser actions, captures screenshots or video, supports proxies, uploads files, and can run page JavaScript.
skill.summary: Automate browser sessions with element refs, screenshots, video, and scripted interactions.
skill.author: toolshell

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown examples, visible shell templates, relative documentation links, and demo URLs. Confirmed risks remain because the skill can capture screens and video, execute page JavaScript, extract cookies, upload local files, and route traffic through SOCKS proxies. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Sensitive screenshots, video, and session artifacts can be captured.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before recording or screenshots, warn about credentials and personal data, and document redaction or deletion steps.

remediation.issue: Documentation teaches cookie extraction from authenticated sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the cookie extraction example and replace it with guidance that forbids collecting, logging, or printing session cookies and tokens.
Remove the Rate Limit Avoidance workflow and require proxy use to follow site terms, consent, and lawful testing boundaries.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary JavaScript execution and file upload can expose sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Add guardrails requiring user approval before execute or upload actions, and warn against selecting secrets, private documents, or restricted page data.

remediation.issue: Executable templates perform networked browser automation and write outputs.
remediation.suggestion: Add template headers that explain required authorization, safe output directories, session cleanup, and restrictions on sensitive pages.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Agent Refs
content.value_statement: Manual web checks and form tasks slow agents down. This skill lets agents navigate pages, use element refs, capture evidence, and run browser actions.
actual_capabilities: Opens browser sessions through the inference.sh agent-browser app.
Returns compact @e element refs for links, buttons, inputs, and other interactive controls.
Clicks, fills, types, selects, scrolls, waits, drags, and uploads files through browser actions.
Captures viewport screenshots, full-page screenshots, and session video recordings.
Runs custom JavaScript in the page context and returns the result.
Routes browser traffic through configured HTTP, HTTPS, or SOCKS proxies.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated inference.sh account.
Element refs can become stale after navigation or dynamic page updates.
Screenshots, video, JavaScript results, and uploaded files can expose sensitive data.
Automation must follow site terms, privacy rules, and user authorization boundaries.

use_cases.title: Validate Web Forms
use_cases.description: Open a form, inspect fields, fill test values, submit it, and capture the result.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Capture screenshots, page text, links, and a recording for a product issue or workflow review.

use_cases.title: Research Interactive Sites
use_cases.description: Navigate pages that need clicks, scrolling, or search input before useful content appears.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this URL with agent-browser, list the visible interactive elements, and tell me which refs are useful for the next step: [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-browser to inspect this form, ask before entering sensitive values, fill the approved fields, submit it, and capture the result: [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Workflow Evidence Pack
prompt_templates.prompt: Record the browser session, complete this workflow, capture screenshots at key states, close the session, and summarize what happened: [WORKFLOW].

prompt_templates.title: Automate an Authenticated Review
prompt_templates.prompt: After I confirm authorization, use agent-browser for this authenticated task. Avoid recording credentials, resnapshot after each navigation, and close the session when done: [TASK].

output_examples.input: Open a pricing page and identify the sign-up button.
output_examples.output: The page opened successfully. The snapshot found navigation links, pricing cards, and a primary sign-up button ref for the next action.

output_examples.input: Capture evidence for a failed checkout flow.
output_examples.output: The session recorded each step, saved screenshots before and after checkout, and reported the visible error message.

output_examples.input: Extract headings and links from a documentation page.
output_examples.output: The browser returned the page title, visible headings, and a concise list of discovered links for review.

best_practices: Get explicit user approval before authenticated browsing, file upload, proxy use, screenshots, or video recording.
Resnapshot after navigation, form submission, dynamic loading, or any action that changes the page.
Close sessions promptly and avoid storing screenshots, videos, cookies, or page text with sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Do not automate sites where you lack authorization or where automation violates terms.
Do not record login pages, passwords, tokens, personal data, or privileged admin screens.
Do not use proxy rotation to evade rate limits, access controls, or regional restrictions.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the web directly?
faq.answer: It uses the inference.sh CLI to run an agent-browser app backed by Playwright-style browser automation.

faq.question: What are @e refs?
faq.answer: They are compact element identifiers returned by snapshots so agents can click or fill specific page controls.

faq.question: Can it handle login flows?
faq.answer: Yes, but users should approve the task and avoid recording or exposing credentials and session cookies.

faq.question: Can it capture video?
faq.answer: Yes. Video is enabled when a session starts and is returned after the session closes.

faq.question: Can it run JavaScript on pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The execute function runs custom JavaScript in the page context, so use it only on authorized pages.

faq.question: Why is this skill high risk?
faq.answer: It can capture screens, run page scripts, upload files, extract cookies, and route traffic through proxies.
